title: When Fine-Grained Credit Assignment Helps and Hurts: Multimodal Agentic Reinforcement Learning through Video Editing
abstract: arXiv:2610.35497v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. However, it remains unclear when fine-grained credit assignment improves learning and when it fails to improve task performance. Video editing provides a useful testbed for this question, combining multimodal perception, long-horizon planning, and tool use with delayed outcome feedback. We construct four movie-trailer editing task types---Content Selection, Narrative Sequencing, Rough Cut, and Fine Cut---that reflect real-world editing workflows and span different levels of task complexity and interaction horizon. Decaying process rewards provides the largest benefit on Fine Cut, with a 45.4% relative gain over outcome-only GRPO on tasks averaging more than 60 turns under outcome-only GRPO. On the three shorter-horizon task types averaging 30--40 turns under the same baseline, outcome-only GRPO remains competitive, with decaying process

translated_title: 细粒度信用分配何时有益何时有害：通过视频剪辑实现的多模态智能体强化学习
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）在训练多模态智能体进行推理和使用工具方面已展现出广阔前景。然而，细粒度信用分配何时能改善学习、何时又无法提升任务性能，这一问题仍不明确。视频剪辑为研究该问题提供了一个理想的测试平台，它融合了多模态感知、长时程规划和工具使用，并伴随着延迟的结果反馈。我们构建了四种电影预告片剪辑任务类型——内容选择、叙事排序、粗剪和精剪——这些任务反映了真实世界的剪辑工作流程，并涵盖了不同层级的任务复杂度与交互时程。衰减式过程奖励在精剪任务上带来了最大的收益，在平均超过60轮的任务上，相比仅使用结果奖励的GRPO取得了45.4%的相对提升。而在同样基线下平均30至40轮的三种较短时程任务类型上，仅使用结果奖励的GRPO依然具有竞争力，衰减式过程……
tldr: 本文通过构建四种电影预告片剪辑任务，系统探究了细粒度信用分配在多模态智能体强化学习中的适用边界，发现衰减式过程奖励在超过60轮的长时程任务（如精剪）上可带来45.4%的显著提升，但在30-40轮的短时程任务上仅结果奖励的GRPO仍具竞争力。
en_tdlr: This paper constructs four movie-trailer editing tasks to systematically investigate when fine-grained credit assignment benefits multimodal agentic RL, showing that decaying process rewards yield a 45.4% relative gain on long-horizon tasks (Fine Cut, 60+ turns), while outcome-only GRPO remains competitive on shorter-horizon tasks averaging 30–40 turns.
